# Inactive simple-position coordinates

Original four-page control generated by `tools/inactive_simple_position_fixture.py`
from the original mixed-cell-anchor fixture. Each foreground picture uses a
10pt column offset and 12pt page offset inside a table cell. `anchor@simplePos`
is explicitly `0` or `false`; the required child has zero, positive, negative or
large unused coordinates. The reference application places every 72 x 36pt image
at (226,86) pt. All four native page images were inspected.

`tools/record_inactive_simple_position.py` extracts frame coordinates, captures
page PNGs and hashes the source and native PDF. Unit tests verify native frames,
hit testing, edits, exact undo, reopening and untouched package parts. Browser
checks compare blue image masks bidirectionally within one pixel before/after
editing and reopening. Malformed coordinates, children, extra attributes and
active simple positioning remain rejected. Original drawing XML is preserved.

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 20.4.2.3 says the anchor's simplePos flag enables the child
coordinates; false leaves positionH/positionV active. Section 20.4.2.13 and
ST_Coordinate define the retained point. This correction accepts signed integer
coordinates within the schema range without applying them to layout. Unit-bearing
coordinate strings and active simple-position layout remain unsupported.

A separate `omitted-flag.docx` changes only the first anchor's simplePos attribute
by omitting it. It passes the transitional schema, and section 20.4.2.3 specifies
that omission disables simple positioning. The reference application instead refuses to
open that control with its generic document-open error. This is an observed
reference/spec divergence; the editor's existing missing-flag rejection is retained
and tested, rather than broadening this fix to omitted flags. No failed native reference PDF
is presented as a reference. Private error log: <work>/omitted-simple-word.log.

No corpus artwork, external renderer, dependency or third-party binary is added.
